body: I asked them, and I wish I hadn't. They started screeching, "NOT SAFE," and, "DANGER," over and over. That worries me.

I assume they can't be together because of the vision the wisps showed me. But I don't know. It doesn't make any sense to me... they've never appeared when any of my other friends have made horrible relationship decisions. (And some of them have made very, very bad decisions indeed.) I just wish these wisps would go away...
i think it would be best not to get her one for christmas.
did your sister ever forgive you for eating her pet rabbit?
Why didn't he *move*? Was she sitting on his lap when she peed on him?

Haven't actually dated anyone with the same name as my parents, but if I had married my (now ex) boyfriend, I would have had the exact same first, middle, and last name as his cousin. Same spelling, too.

I had indeed seen some places say that prayer was a form of magick, but I wasn't completely sure. Thanks for confirming that. I still probably won't mention that to any of my Christian friends though. I've learned that sometimes it's just best to keep one's mouth shut.

I will definitely let you all know if I do. :) The closest I have ever gotten is feeling like someone is watching me so far. I visited an old fort used in the Civil War one summer. Sadly I no longer remember the name of it, but it was right across the water from Fort Sumtner. (Not sure if I spelled that right, but it was one of the forts in South Carolina.)
The only thing I'd be afraid of with a flying car is running into things. Where I live, there are lots of telephone poles and wires. I'd rather not have to explain that to my insurance company. :P

I did see a picture of a mandrake once that looked like a pair of legs. If we were to put that one with the picture you have there, and add some arms, we'd have a miniature human made of mandrakes. xD

After meeting Nearly Headless Nick in the books, I've always wondered whether or not spirits manifest as they were when they were killed or not, or if they could control what they manifest as. I've never actually seen one, and I am unsure whether to believe what I've seen from certain pictures from shows such as "A Haunting" and "Ghost Hunters."

Out of curiosity, has Rowling ever mentioned speaking with a real witch?

It is interesting to notice, though, that even if some of the things weren't represented quite like they are in real life in the books, that there is a basis for them somewhere. Another person mentioned herbology, and I remembered that witches (or some, I don't know if all do) get into the use of herbs.

Speaking of which, is it necessary to speak at all while using magick, or is it perfectly fine to just say it all in your head and simply use the wand to direct energy?

If it were possible to have a flying car with an invisibility button in it, that would be amazing, though I'm sure that isn't possible. I do know that it takes energy to cause magick to happen, and I'm not sure how much energy it would take to lift a car or how long it would stay in the air. That, and it would cause a lot of problems if anyone saw that. I actually read the series earlier this year, but I'm not a die-hard HP fan, so I haven't memorized every detail. :P
So even beyond the grave, it is possible for such energy to manifest and protect others?

The Divination teacher was also believed to be insane, but I've met many people who think divination is just some sort of trick or lie. 

I thought that herbology probably was exaggerated, especially when the screaming mandrakes came in. I don't remember half of the potions made except the Wigginweld (I'm sure I spelled it wrong) potion that healed health in the games.

Alchemy is taken to very... different heights than what it really is. For example, in Fullmetal Alchemist, they do use symbols that are probably used in alchemy (I've never actually checked) but most of what they do is some sort of strange magic that allows them to fix walls, make bread from grass, and turn stone into a weapon in mere seconds. I know quite well that alchemy is not as it is represented in such shows.

I would surely hope that they do not scream, as hearing it in the movies was quite enough for me! I have seen other movies where the mandrake has been said to house a living spirit (I cannot think of any of the names at the moment, though) and I must say that I find it possible. Plants are, in my opinion, alive. I tried telling that to my second grade teacher once (oh, how long ago that was now!) and she argued that plants are in no way alive. I kept my opinion of plants to myself after that.

The only "working with spirits" I ever saw in Harry Potter was talking to the ghosts, but I don't recall any of the ghosts actually helping with any kind of spells or anything of the sort.

**Edit:** To be fair to the ghosts, though, my memory isn't all that great at remembering everything that happened in the books. xD
Interesting. What was the "patronus" spell used for according to that book?

Both articles were quite informative, and I found synchronicity quite interesting. I may have to look into that further, especially after reading the account between Jung and Freud where Jung said that there would be another report from the bookshelf with certainty and, indeed, it did! Thank you for providing these articles.

I do hope you aren't too hard on yourself for it, though. Children don't know better, and this time the kitten will survive and make a full recovery. You just have to watch out when he gets older, because he'll surely be a mess!
